newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Samancor H1 shr seen crumbling.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Samancor H1 shr seen crumbling.

text.p: Low international ferro-alloy prices will take a heavy toll on the first half earnings at Samancor Ltd, analysts said on Tuesday.
"I am looking for a huge drop in earnings to about 90 cents per share," one analyst, who did not want to be identified, told Reuters.
"Samancor is mainly a manganese and chrome producer and manganese follows the trend in steel output in the world which last year went down by one percent."

Analysts polled by Reuters said Samancor was likely to report earnings per share of between 90 to 110 cents, down from 161 in the corresponding 1995 period, when it announces its results for the six months to end-December on Monday.
Views were split as to whether Samancor would cut its dividend.
Some analysts are looking for a reduction to as little as 42 cents but other predicted the company would hold the payout at 60 cents, the same as in the first half of 1995.

George Grohmann of stockbroker Rice Rinaldi commented: "The way things are going at the moment the ferro-alloys market has been fairly down in the last six months of last year...but they (Samancor) are absorbing losses from Columbus as well."
Columbus is a joint venture between Samancor Ltd, the state's Industrial Development Corporation and Highveld Steel and Vanadium Ltd.

The plant -- one of the world's biggest stainless steel producers -- opened in February 1996. But Grohmann said problems experienced in the middle of last year at Columbus' Middelburg plant would impact badly on Samancor's interim earnings.
But despite the gloomy outlook for first half results, some analysts saw recovery potential for the company with steel production set to increase by close to two percent in 1997.
"I think if we look into 1998 their results will be up -- they will pick to some degree," said one analyst.
